posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I disabled the "send e-mail" notifications since I'm usually decently active on the forum that it would just be spam.  I'm not sure how many other users do that.
But, even if posts are merged, it should still give you the red "notification" alert in the upper right hand corner unless you've disabled that.  I've had threads I was in still give me alerts when they were merged.
Tagging someone specifically also produces that red alert at the top.
I can see it would be a problem for those who rarely ever visit the site, though.  Just throw a random question into the void, and no e-mail to let you know it was ever answered, so you can come back and read it...  That would be an issue.

I mean, that SOUNDS good... ON PAPER... But in practice?
I do a search for a specific problem on google or something.  It pulls me into the existing support thread with no solution on it.  It doesn't pull me into any "solution thread" on it, because I didn't search the exact text (or similar enough text) to the solution or the reply with the solution.
So, creating a new thread with the solution that just links back to the original thread... is... fairly useless.  Unless you're going to just hit "quote" on that original thread, post the quote into a new thread, and then your reply under it.
From a search engine standpoint, it's probably better to allow necro-ing of posts where no solution to a problem was given, because then people using google or yahoo or whatever else can find the thread and the solution without having to ask again.
Sure, it doesn't help anyone who frequents these forums... but it's not like someone looking for a solution to a single problem is joining our forums anyway, except to ask about their one issue and move along.  Not everyone who uses these forums wants to join the community or even interact with the community.  I would propose that most people who pass through this website are "here for a quick fix" and then never return.  Especially if they don't see a solution to their question here.  Those of us who stick around and frequently post are the extremely vast and very vocal minority of users of these programs.  Whether we like that or not.

Click to expand...
Ok but can you please explain to us how necroposting in order to contribute a valid answer -- even if your answer has a slightly different target (
like if the OP asks about image assets not loading in on game load on a PC build but you go and give a relevant answer to the OP's question but from the context of Android builds but also includes info about the context of a PC build
) -- how does that count as "disruptive" exactly?
In that example, you're still contributing valid information to the conversation in the thread, but just because it was a response that was 2 years late to the convo it suddenly becomes a bad thing?
Sorry but that's not how real world convos work boss. Just because you're late to the public online convo doesn't automatically make it irrelevant info being contributed to the convo and even if the OP hasn't responded doesn't mean the convo is over... it just means THAT person got what THEY wanted out of the convo and there could still be others who didn't get what they were looking for.
Also, to tell us users to make a new thread when there is already an existing thread that just been silent for a long while.... that sounds like a waste of time and more cleanup work for the mods and a completely disorganized/chaotic/messy way to organize the info made available to the public via what should've been a single thread that is dedicated to that 1 topic. If we create a new thread simply because the existing thread was supposedly "silent/inactive for too long" defeats the purpose of having a dedicated source of info on a single topic.
So my question for the staff of this forum is two fold:
1st - Is posting in a thread that has been silent/inactive for a while -- also known as "necroposting" -- with additional info to contribute to the existing convo (given the dictionary definition of the word "conversation") actually a valid example of what you call "disruptive posting"?
2nd - Given the examples and reasoning I've shared in this post, is there any valid reason to still keep the rule that forbids "necroposting" in this official RPG Maker forum given the fact that users of RPG Maker come here an use this forum as a library of sorts? If a library of info on the very game engines this forum is meant to support is disorganized due to an erroneous rule such as "No Necroposting" forcing the users who post useful info here in these threads to "create a new thread" to continue the conversation related to the topic said thread is dedicated to... well that wouldn't make the library very useful now would it?
If that rule is not promoting a positive user experience and is leading to an obstruction of users in their search for the info they seek, then I strongly suggest you remove it.
Seeing as users, like myself and others here in this current thread for example, are complaining about the "No Necroposting" rule and the similar/related rules to this rule, then that is more than enough proof that it needs to be removed due to it clearly causing a negative user experience. Is that not what you are understanding our complaints about these types of rules to be? Speaking from a user myself, this is deffo a community outcry for such rules to be removed. I don't know how it could possibly be any more clear than it already is...

"Hey, remember that time we broke up because we argued about how to get a game to run on android?"
I don't know what planet you are from here, but pretty sure that's not how "real world convo" works.
Kurochan said:
can you please explain to us how necroposting in order to contribute a valid answer -- even if your answer has a slightly different target
Click to expand...
In no particular order:
Many topics get replied to by recent posting on here. By replying to an older one you bump another topic out of sight which might result in someone going unanswered.
The advice provided in the topic, unless wholly relevant to the original point, would add noise and frustration to anyone who is actually looking up the situation they are trying to troubleshoot.
Users who might have been involved with that thread will get a ping for it, which may clutter their notifications.
The original author of the thread may get a ping for the thread when the information is no longer valuable; in a way it could almost be insulting to them.
If you have genuinely useful advice, obscuring it in an old thread makes it mostly pointless. However I'll come back to that point. Put a pin in it. But otherwise, you can just can just create another thread (such as a tutorial) if you think the information is important. A new thread would appear better in search results.
If you are bumping an older thread still seeking an answer or asking a follow-up question, less people are going to see it and reply to it; it is faster and better to create a new topic and link back to the old topic for additional context.
It's annoying seeing old topics from months or even years ago crop back up.
bots might add spam to old threads - could happen to any thread, new or old, but let's not give them more vectors.
About that thing I told you to put a pin in:
There have been a few rare occasions people have posted answers to long dead threads with a genuinely helpful and informative piece of advice that fit the main topic's question - assuming the topic never got a satisfying answer before. Often that is appreciated, and while they might still receive blue text for necroing, I need to reiterate the point I made on your profile post on the admin's profile:
Blue text does not equal warning points. You are not being punished, you are just being informed of the rules.
The funny part is that
@Canned_Dinosaur
already brought this point up in the topic earlier. Dang, if I had a nickel for every time it felt like you didn't actually read things I'd have a dime and 5 pennies.
Kurochan said:
make a new thread when there is already an existing thread
Click to expand...
Because of the way posts are made in a linear chronological order it means that typically most people coming into a long thread with many posts will only read the first and last page.
If people constantly tacked on new information to an old thread, it would become bloated and difficult to sort out what the most helpful information is for the user searching it. There is no new additional mess made for mods when creating a new thread unless people start acting belligerent or making erroneous pompous claims because they feel slighted.
Kurochan said:
1st - Is posting in a thread that has been silent/inactive for a while -- also known as "necroposting" -- with additional info to contribute to the existing convo (given the dictionary definition of the word "conversation") actually a valid example of what you call "disruptive posting"?
Click to expand...
Mods can give a more nuanced answer, but I can promise you it's going to boil down to:
"Yes."
Kurochan said:
2nd - Given the examples and reasoning I've shared in this post, is there any valid reason to still keep the rule that forbids "necroposting" in this official RPG Maker forum given the fact that users of RPG Maker come here an use this forum as a library of sorts? If a library of info on the very game engines this forum is meant to support is disorganized due to an erroneous rule such as "No Necroposting" forcing the users who post useful info here in these threads to "create a new thread" to continue the conversation related to the topic said thread is dedicated to... well that wouldn't make the library very useful now would it?
Click to expand...
What is more erroneous is your claim of disorganization; you'd need to provide examples of that. How is it any more "disorganized" than any other message board?
And while you might use it as a library - and it certainly is a benefit of it's history - it is first and foremost a place to request help with the game engine.
Burying your info in an old thread instead of writing a "Kurochan's Cool Tips and Tricks you might not have known about" thread is less useful. Using your library metaphor; imagine someone stuck a piece of paper with notes jotted on it in one of the many books about birds as opposed to them writing a new book with their new discovery on birds to add to the library.
The fact of the matter is you have
1) Framed this place incorrectly, as it is not built to be an archive first. It is built to be a place to request support first.
2) You are being overly reactive to a meaningless bit of blue text and stirring the pot over nothing. Everyone has been blue-texted before, it doesn't mean you're grounded.
For christ sake, give it a rest; your information wasn't deleted, you didn't get warning points, there was no trouble. You're making a mountain out of a molehill and it's embarrassing.
edit:
Added a new point someone mentioned earlier in this thread (the irony of you complaining about necroing and then going to an older thread).
Once again, if you would read, just like you didn't with the rules I had linked earlier - there are only like 2, maybe 3 people complaining about the rules when there are 200k users on this forum. That's not an outcry, that's a family complaining to the Burger King their fries weren't cooked enough.

I could cite several examples, but I'll list the most pertinent:
1.  People generally ignore the solution if given too long ago.  In effect, you're screaming into the void.  If I never come back to these forums after asking for help, I never get the help I asked for.
2.  Your solution could also be irrelevent.  You might think "It's the right answer", but without the original poster telling you "Yep, that solved it!", it's also useless and screaming into the void.
3.  There's been more than once someone has "necro'd" a post that wasn't subject to necro rules, from several years ago, and I had accidently thought it was "a new topic" only to find I'd already replied to the subject... and it had last been relevant 3 or more years ago.  It wasn't some new take on an old and well-tread subject.  It was just someone throwing in their point of view on an already dead subject.  Which... basically meant the reply got no real responses at all.
It would've been far better to make a new discussion so the user could've got replies.  Especially as the context for the original post had been dead more than 3 years.
I felt no need to "update" such a thread with "my new perspective" (people change, shocker!), since I'd already replied to the thread 3 years ago.  But, if a new post had been made on the subject, someone might have gotten my "current year perspective" on the subject.  If they cared about such things.
